doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Residuals, the after contract and the power of yes
summary: Refusing a buyout earned residuals; he credits a Christmas party gig and saying yes; Rowe mentions Phil Woods.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Yeah you’re going to get — “we would like to offer you X amount of dollars for this.” And Sunny said to me, she took me aside and said, “Man, we ought to hold out for an after contract in case this thing does go so that we could get residuals on it.” So we went to the producer and we said we’d really like an after contract. And they went, fortunately, “no problem.” And because of that, and I’ve written Sunny many times and I said, “Sunny, thank you, thank you for having the smarts and the foresight to just ask that we do this legitimately, not take the buyout, do the after contract. And that show is still paying me some mailbox money every year. It afforded me a little bit of a nice little pension through AFTRA and it blew up worldwide. So in the early 90s I was getting residual checks from it being shown in Italy and all over the planet. It was probably the most lucrative hour and a half of my life. And a complete fluke. I just truly right place, right time. I happened to play a Christmas party where this guy heard me sing “Mustang Sally” or something and remembered my name because he hired the band I was in because he was good friends with the drummer in the band. So he called my friend Doug and Doug gave him my number and the dot is connected and that’s how that all went down.

I love those stories because you think about the young musicians now and most of them are going the academic route, and say how do you get a break. Well? Play a Christmas party. You never know what’s going to happen.

Exactly. Yes is the most important word I think a musician can have in their vocabulary because you never know. And though you may be tempted to go, like the thing with Christopher, I almost went oh man there’s no rehearsal bread there’s nothing. I’m so happy I said yeah I’ll do it.
You know Phil Woods had a great story about that. He opted just to get the money for the Billy Joel thing with “Just the Way You Are.”
Or maybe he wasn’t even aware of it.
Well, live and learn I guess.
